Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Offshore Energy Installation Safety Directive (OEISD) below. No regulator summary has been provided.

---
PRIOR TEXT — OEISD Edition 3, Articles 1–7
---

Article 1. Scope
This Directive applies to all offshore energy installations operating within the Exclusive Economic Zone of Veldrath, including fixed platforms, floating production units, and subsea infrastructure with a rated power output exceeding 5 MW.

Article 2. Safety Case Submission
Operators shall submit a Safety Case to the Veldrath Offshore Safety Authority (VOSA) at least 180 days before commencing production operations. The Safety Case shall describe all major hazard scenarios and the control measures in place.

Article 3. Competency Assurance
Operators shall maintain a competency assurance framework for all personnel engaged in safety-critical activities. The framework shall include regular assessment of individual competency against defined role requirements.

Article 4. Emergency Response Plan
Operators shall prepare and maintain an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) covering well control, fire, explosion, and hydrocarbon release scenarios. The ERP shall be reviewed at intervals not exceeding 24 months.

Article 5. Well Notification
Prior to the commencement of any well operation, operators shall notify VOSA in writing at least 21 days in advance, providing the well programme and the identity of the well operator.

Article 6. Incident Reporting
Operators shall report to VOSA any dangerous occurrence or occupational injury resulting in absence from work exceeding three consecutive days. Reports shall be submitted within 72 hours of the operator becoming aware of the incident.

Article 7. Records Retention
Operators shall retain all records required under this Directive for a minimum period of five years from the date of creation.

---
NEW TEXT — OEISD Edition 4, Articles 1–8
---

Article 1. Scope
This Directive applies to all offshore energy installations operating within the Exclusive Economic Zone of Veldrath, including fixed platforms, floating production units, subsea infrastructure, and floating offshore wind installations, with a rated power output exceeding 5 MW.

Article 2. Safety Case Submission
Operators shall submit a Safety Case to the Veldrath Offshore Safety Authority (VOSA) at least 180 days before commencing production operations. The Safety Case shall describe all major hazard scenarios and the control measures in place.

Article 3. Competency Assurance
Operators shall maintain a competency assurance framework for all personnel engaged in safety-critical activities. The framework shall include regular assessment of individual competency against defined role requirements and shall be reviewed at intervals not exceeding 36 months.

Article 4. Emergency Response Plan
Operators shall prepare and maintain an Emergency Response Plan (ERP) covering well control, fire, explosion, hydrocarbon release, and structural failure scenarios. The ERP shall be reviewed at intervals not exceeding 24 months.

Article 5. Well Notification
Prior to the commencement of any well operation, operators shall notify VOSA in writing at least 21 days in advance, providing the well programme, the identity of the well operator, and a summary of the proposed well integrity management measures.

Article 6. Incident Reporting
Operators shall report to VOSA any dangerous occurrence or occupational injury resulting in absence from work exceeding three consecutive days. Reports shall be submitted within 72 hours of the operator becoming aware of the incident.

Article 7. Contractor Safety Obligations
Where operations are carried out wholly or partly by contractors, operators shall ensure that contractors operating safety-critical equipment maintain a competency assurance framework equivalent to that required under Article 3.

Article 8. Records Retention
Operators shall retain all records required under this Directive for a minimum period of five years from the date of creation.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Veldrath Consumer Credit Disclosure Rules (VCCDR) below. A regulator-issued change summary is included.

---
REGULATOR SUMMARY (Veldrath Financial Services Commission, Circular FSC-2026-14)
---
"The amendments to the VCCDR published in this circular clarify existing disclosure obligations and align the Rules with established supervisory guidance. In particular, the addition of Article 4(c) clarifies what information must be presented prominently. No new substantive obligations are introduced."

---
PRIOR TEXT — VCCDR, Articles 1–5
---

Article 1. Application
These Rules apply to all persons providing consumer credit in Veldrath, including banks, credit unions, and licensed non-bank lenders.

Article 2. Pre-Contractual Disclosure
Before entering into a consumer credit agreement, a lender shall provide the borrower with a standardised pre-contractual information statement containing the total cost of credit, the annual percentage rate, and the repayment schedule.

Article 3. Advertising Standards
Any advertisement for a consumer credit product shall state the annual percentage rate prominently and shall not use misleading comparisons.

Article 4. Contract Terms
(a) Credit agreements shall be set out in plain language accessible to the target consumer.
(b) Any fees or charges not included in the annual percentage rate shall be separately itemised in the agreement.

Article 5. Complaints Handling
Lenders shall maintain a complaints handling procedure and shall resolve complaints within 45 business days of receipt.

---
NEW TEXT — VCCDR (amended), Articles 1–5
---

Article 1. Application
These Rules apply to all persons providing consumer credit in Veldrath, including banks, credit unions, licensed non-bank lenders, and buy-now-pay-later service providers.

Article 2. Pre-Contractual Disclosure
Before entering into a consumer credit agreement, a lender shall provide the borrower with a standardised pre-contractual information statement containing the total cost of credit, the annual percentage rate, and the repayment schedule.

Article 3. Advertising Standards
Any advertisement for a consumer credit product shall state the annual percentage rate prominently and shall not use misleading comparisons.

Article 4. Contract Terms
(a) Credit agreements shall be set out in plain language accessible to the target consumer.
(b) Any fees or charges not included in the annual percentage rate shall be separately itemised in the agreement.
(c) The annual percentage rate and total cost of credit shall be displayed in a font size no smaller than the largest font size used elsewhere in the agreement.

Article 5. Complaints Handling
Lenders shall maintain a complaints handling procedure and shall resolve complaints within 30 business days of receipt.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Medtravar Pharmaceutical Serialisation and Track-and-Trace Requirements (PSTR) below. A regulator explanatory note is included.

---
REGULATOR EXPLANATORY NOTE (Medtravar Medicines Regulatory Agency, MRA-EN-2025-09)
---
"Articles 3 and 4 have been restructured for clarity. The obligations they contain are unchanged; the restructuring reflects supervisory practice as already communicated in MRA Supervisory Letter SL-2023-04, which required manufacturers to notify the MRA of any serialisation system failure within 48 hours."

---
PRIOR TEXT — PSTR, Articles 1–6
---

Article 1. Definitions
"Serialisation" means the assignment of a unique identifier to each saleable unit of a medicinal product.

Article 2. Scope
These Requirements apply to all manufacturers and marketing authorisation holders placing medicinal products on the Medtravar market.

Article 3. Serialisation Obligation
Manufacturers shall assign a unique identifier to each saleable unit before the product is released for distribution.

Article 4. System Integrity
Manufacturers shall take appropriate measures to ensure the integrity of their serialisation systems.

Article 5. Wholesale Distributor Verification
Wholesale distributors shall verify the unique identifier of each medicinal product at the point of receipt from the manufacturer and at the point of supply to a pharmacy or hospital.

Article 6. Records
All parties subject to these Requirements shall maintain records of serialisation transactions for a minimum of three years.

---
NEW TEXT — PSTR (revised), Articles 1–7
---

Article 1. Definitions
"Serialisation" means the assignment of a unique identifier to each saleable unit of a medicinal product.

Article 2. Scope
These Requirements apply to all manufacturers and marketing authorisation holders placing medicinal products on the Medtravar market.

Article 3. Serialisation Obligation
Manufacturers shall assign a unique identifier to each saleable unit before the product is released for distribution.

Article 4. System Integrity
Manufacturers shall take appropriate measures to ensure the integrity of their serialisation systems, including: conducting quarterly system validation tests; maintaining documented procedures for system failure response; and notifying the Medtravar Medicines Regulatory Agency within 48 hours of any system failure that affects the assignment or verification of unique identifiers.

Article 5. Wholesale Distributor Verification
Wholesale distributors shall verify the unique identifier of each medicinal product at the point of receipt from the manufacturer and at the point of supply to a pharmacy or hospital.

Article 6. Marketing Authorisation Holder Audit Rights
Marketing authorisation holders shall conduct or commission an annual audit of the serialisation systems of any contract manufacturer producing medicinal products on their behalf.

Article 7. Records
All parties subject to these Requirements shall maintain records of serialisation transactions for a minimum of three years.

Please extract the obligation delta for the following regulatory texts. Note that only the new text has been provided.

---
NEW TEXT — Belcorian Data Residency Ordinance (BDRO), Articles 1–6 (2026 Revision)
---

Article 1. Purpose
This Ordinance establishes data residency requirements for personal data of Belcorian residents processed by digital service providers.

Article 2. Scope
This Ordinance applies to digital service providers with more than 10,000 active Belcorian user accounts.

Article 3. Data Residency Obligation
Personal data of Belcorian residents shall be stored on servers physically located within the territory of Belcor.

Article 4. Transfer Restriction
Personal data shall not be transferred outside Belcor unless the recipient jurisdiction has been designated as adequate by the Belcorian Data Authority.

Article 5. Audit Right
The Belcorian Data Authority may conduct or commission audits of digital service providers to verify compliance with Articles 3 and 4.

Article 6. Penalties
Breaches of this Ordinance may result in fines of up to 2% of global annual turnover.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Narrath Waste Classification and Disposal Regulations (WCDR) below. A regulator change summary is included.

---
REGULATOR CHANGE SUMMARY (Narrath Environmental Standards Office, ESO Notice 2026-03)
---
"The amendment to WCDR Regulation 5 removes the small-quantity generator exemption. This amendment clarifies the scope of the Regulation by aligning it with the treatment of small-quantity generators under the Narrath Hazardous Materials Framework (NHMF), which already subjected them to equivalent obligations."

---
PRIOR TEXT — WCDR, Regulations 1–6
---

Regulation 1. Interpretation
"Hazardous waste" means any waste that exhibits ignitability, corrosivity, reactivity, or toxicity as defined in Schedule A.

Regulation 2. Waste Manifest
All persons generating hazardous waste shall complete a waste manifest before transferring hazardous waste to a licensed carrier.

Regulation 3. Licensed Carrier Requirement
Hazardous waste shall only be transported by carriers holding a valid licence issued by the Narrath Environmental Standards Office.

Regulation 4. Treatment and Disposal
Hazardous waste shall be treated and disposed of at a facility authorised by the Narrath Environmental Standards Office.

Regulation 5. Scope Exemption
Regulations 2, 3, and 4 shall not apply to small-quantity generators, being persons generating less than 25 kilograms of hazardous waste per calendar month.

Regulation 6. Records
All persons subject to these Regulations shall maintain records of waste manifests and disposal certificates for a minimum of four years.

---
NEW TEXT — WCDR (amended), Regulations 1–5
---

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Calveth Investment Adviser Conduct Standards (CIACS) below. No regulator summary has been provided.

---
PRIOR TEXT — CIACS, Standards 1–7
---

Standard 1. Fiduciary Duty
Investment advisers shall act in the best interests of their clients and shall disclose any material conflicts of interest.

Standard 2. Suitability Assessment
Before making a recommendation, investment advisers shall assess whether the recommended product or strategy is suitable for the client, having regard to the client's financial situation, investment objectives, and risk tolerance.

Standard 3. Client Agreement
Investment advisers shall enter into a written client agreement before providing advice. The agreement shall set out the basis of the adviser's remuneration.

Standard 4. Record of Advice
Investment advisers shall maintain a record of each recommendation made and the basis for it.

Standard 5. Continuing Education
Investment advisers shall complete a minimum of 20 hours of continuing professional education per calendar year, at least 10 of which must relate to the Calveth regulatory framework.

Standard 6. Complaint Escalation
Where a complaint is not resolved within 30 days, the investment adviser shall notify the Calveth Financial Conduct Authority (CFCA) and provide a summary of the complaint and steps taken.

Standard 7. Record Retention
All records required under these Standards shall be retained for a minimum of seven years.

---
NEW TEXT — CIACS (revised), Standards 1–7
---

Standard 1. Fiduciary Duty
Investment advisers shall act in the best interests of their clients and shall disclose any material conflicts of interest.

Standard 2. Suitability Assessment
Before making a recommendation, investment advisers shall assess whether the recommended product or strategy is suitable for the client, having regard to the client's financial situation, investment objectives, risk tolerance, and sustainability preferences.

Standard 3. Client Agreement
Investment advisers shall enter into a written client agreement before providing advice. The agreement shall set out the basis of the adviser's remuneration.

Standard 4. Record of Advice
Investment advisers shall maintain a record of each recommendation made, the basis for it, and a note of any sustainability preferences expressed by the client and how those preferences were taken into account.

Standard 5. Continuing Education
Investment advisers shall complete a minimum of 20 hours of continuing professional education per calendar year, at least 10 of which must relate to the Calveth regulatory framework.

Standard 6. Complaint Escalation
Where a complaint is not resolved within 60 days, the investment adviser shall notify the Calveth Financial Conduct Authority (CFCA) and provide a summary of the complaint and steps taken.

Standard 7. Record Retention
All records required under these Standards shall be retained for a minimum of seven years.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Ferrath Grid Operator Balancing Obligations (GOBO) below. No regulator summary has been provided.

---
PRIOR TEXT — GOBO, Sections 1–5
---

Section 1. Definitions
"Imbalance" means the difference between a market participant's declared schedule and its actual metered position during a settlement period.

Section 2. Balancing Notification
Market participants shall submit balancing notifications to the Ferrath Grid Operator (FGO) covering each settlement period no later than 60 minutes before the start of that period.

Section 3. Imbalance Settlement
The FGO shall calculate each market participant's imbalance for each settlement period and shall apply the imbalance settlement price published for that period.

Section 4. Metering Data Submission
Market participants shall submit metered data to the FGO within 10 business days of the end of each month.

Section 5. Record Keeping
Market participants shall retain records of all balancing notifications and metered data submissions for a period of six years.

---
NEW TEXT — GOBO (amended), Sections 1–5
---

Section 1. Definitions
"Imbalance" means the difference between a market participant's declared schedule and its actual metered position during a settlement period. "Aggregator" means a person who combines the flexible capacity of multiple end-users and participates in balancing markets on their behalf.

Section 2. Balancing Notification
Market participants, including aggregators acting on behalf of end-users, shall submit balancing notifications to the Ferrath Grid Operator (FGO) covering each settlement period no later than 60 minutes before the start of that period.

Section 3. Imbalance Settlement
The FGO shall calculate each market participant's imbalance for each settlement period and shall apply the imbalance settlement price published for that period.

Section 4. Metering Data Submission
Market participants shall submit metered data to the FGO within 10 business days of the end of each month.

Section 5. Record Keeping
Market participants shall retain records of all balancing notifications and metered data submissions for a period of six years.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Relpath Food Safety Labelling Code (FSLC) below. A regulator advisory note is included.

---
REGULATOR ADVISORY NOTE (Relpath Food Standards Bureau, FSB Advisory 2025-11)
---
"Sections 3 and 4 have been renumbered as Sections 4 and 5 respectively following the insertion of a new Section 3 on allergen declarations. The substantive text of the renumbered provisions is unchanged."

---
PRIOR TEXT — FSLC, Sections 1–5
---

Section 1. Scope
This Code applies to all food business operators placing pre-packaged food products on the Relpath market.

Section 2. Mandatory Information
Pre-packaged food products shall display the following information on the label: product name; list of ingredients; net quantity; best-before or use-by date; name and address of the food business operator; and country of origin.

Section 3. Nutrition Declaration
A nutrition declaration shall be provided for all pre-packaged food products, setting out energy value, amounts of fat, saturated fat, carbohydrate, sugars, protein, and salt per 100g or 100ml.

Section 4. Language Requirements
Labels shall be in the official language of Relpath. A second language may be used in addition.

Section 5. Records
Food business operators shall retain labelling records for a minimum of two years after the product ceases to be placed on the market.

---
NEW TEXT — FSLC (amended), Sections 1–6
---

Section 1. Scope
This Code applies to all food business operators placing pre-packaged food products on the Relpath market.

Section 2. Mandatory Information
Pre-packaged food products shall display the following information on the label: product name; list of ingredients; net quantity; best-before or use-by date; name and address of the food business operator; and country of origin.

Section 3. Allergen Declaration
Where a pre-packaged food product contains any of the substances listed in Annex B, the allergen shall be declared on the label in a typeface or colour that is visually distinct from the remainder of the ingredients list.

Section 4. Nutrition Declaration (was: Section 3)
A nutrition declaration shall be provided for all pre-packaged food products, setting out energy value, amounts of fat, saturated fat, carbohydrate, sugars, protein, and salt per 100g or 100ml.

Section 5. Language Requirements (was: Section 4)
Labels shall be in the official language of Relpath. A second language may be used in addition.

Section 6. Records (was: Section 5)
Food business operators shall retain labelling records for a minimum of two years after the product ceases to be placed on the market.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Dravani Construction Product Certification Scheme (CPCS) below. No regulator summary has been provided.

---
PRIOR TEXT — CPCS, Clauses 1–6
---

Clause 1. Purpose and Scope
This Scheme applies to manufacturers of load-bearing construction products placed on the Dravani market.

Clause 2. Conformity Assessment
Before placing a load-bearing construction product on the market, manufacturers shall obtain a conformity assessment from a Scheme-approved third-party body confirming that the product meets the applicable performance standards.

Clause 3. Certification Mark
Products that have undergone conformity assessment under Clause 2 may bear the Dravani Certification Mark.

Clause 4. Market Surveillance Cooperation
Manufacturers shall cooperate with market surveillance inspections carried out by the Dravani Construction Products Authority (DCPA) and shall provide requested documentation within 14 business days of any request.

Clause 5. Defect Notification
Where a manufacturer becomes aware that a product it has placed on the market does not conform to the performance standards, it shall notify the DCPA within 7 days and shall withdraw the product from the market within 30 days unless the DCPA directs otherwise.

Clause 6. Record Keeping
Manufacturers shall retain conformity assessment certificates and supporting technical documentation for a minimum of 10 years from the date of last supply of the product.

---
NEW TEXT — CPCS (amended), Clauses 1–6
---

Clause 1. Purpose and Scope
This Scheme applies to manufacturers and importers of load-bearing construction products placed on the Dravani market.

Clause 2. Conformity Assessment
Before placing a load-bearing construction product on the market, manufacturers and importers shall obtain a conformity assessment from a Scheme-approved third-party body confirming that the product meets the applicable performance standards.

Clause 3. Certification Mark
Products that have undergone conformity assessment under Clause 2 may bear the Dravani Certification Mark.

Clause 4. Market Surveillance Cooperation
Manufacturers and importers shall cooperate with market surveillance inspections carried out by the Dravani Construction Products Authority (DCPA) and shall provide requested documentation within 14 business days of any request.

Clause 5. Defect Notification
Where a manufacturer or importer becomes aware that a product it has placed on the market does not conform to the performance standards, it shall notify the DCPA within 7 days and shall withdraw the product from the market within 30 days unless the DCPA directs otherwise.

Clause 6. Record Keeping
Manufacturers and importers shall retain conformity assessment certificates and supporting technical documentation for a minimum of 10 years from the date of last supply of the product.

Please extract the obligation delta between the two versions of the Sentavo Electronic Communications Interception Rules (ECIR) below. A regulator explanatory memorandum is included.

---
REGULATOR EXPLANATORY MEMORANDUM (Sentavo Communications Authority, SCA-EM-2026-02)
---
"Article 4 has been amended to require providers to document their lawful interception capability assessments. This requirement reflects the existing obligation under SCA Operational Guidance OG-2024-17 to maintain such assessments and aligns the written Rules with established practice."

---
PRIOR TEXT — ECIR, Articles 1–5
---

Article 1. Scope
These Rules apply to publicly available electronic communications service providers operating networks in Sentavo.

Article 2. Lawful Interception Capability
Providers shall maintain the technical and organisational capability to intercept electronic communications upon receipt of a valid authority issued by the Sentavo Security Directorate.

Article 3. Interception Handover Interface
Providers shall maintain a handover interface conforming to the technical specifications published by the Sentavo Communications Authority.

Article 4. Capability Assessment
Providers shall assess their lawful interception capability at intervals not exceeding 12 months and shall take corrective action where deficiencies are identified.

Article 5. Confidentiality
Providers shall not disclose to any person other than the Sentavo Security Directorate the existence or content of any interception authority.

---
NEW TEXT — ECIR (amended), Articles 1–6
---

Article 1. Scope
These Rules apply to publicly available electronic communications service providers operating networks in Sentavo.

Article 2. Lawful Interception Capability
Providers shall maintain the technical and organisational capability to intercept electronic communications upon receipt of a valid authority issued by the Sentavo Security Directorate.

Article 3. Interception Handover Interface
Providers shall maintain a handover interface conforming to the technical specifications published by the Sentavo Communications Authority.

Article 4. Capability Assessment
Providers shall assess their lawful interception capability at intervals not exceeding 12 months, shall document each assessment in a written report, and shall take corrective action where deficiencies are identified.

Article 5. New Provider Notification
A provider that commences operation of a new network segment shall notify the Sentavo Communications Authority within 30 days and shall submit a capability assessment for the new segment within 90 days of commencement.

Article 6. Confidentiality
Providers shall not disclose to any person other than the Sentavo Security Directorate the existence or content of any interception authority.
